previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and sharp chest pain over the prior three days, initially raising concern for reaccumulation of pericardial effusion. She had been hospitalized a month earlier for pericardial effusion of unknown etiology. Evaluation revealed new pulmonary venous congestion on chest X-ray and elevated proBNP, consistent with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure. There was no evidence of myocardial infarction, and bedside ultrasound showed no significant pericardial effusion. A repeat echocardiogram confirmed a small, stable pericardial effusion with no hemodynamic compromise. She was treated with increased furosemide dosing, which improved her symptoms and resolved pulmonary rales. A weakly positive urinalysis led to a short course of ciprofloxacin for asymptomatic UTI. She remained stable, was discharged home on increased diuresis, and advised to monitor weight and continue outpatient work-up for possible malignancy and shoulder pain.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with history of cervical fracture, now status
post mechanical fall, here to evaluate for cervical fracture.

COMPARISON:  CT of C-spine, last performed on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained of the
cervical spine.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were reviewed.

FINDINGS:  A type II dens fracture is redemonstrated with a single threaded
screw transfixing the slightly displaced odontoid process fracture fragments. 
There is increased lucency at the tip of the screw compared to the prior ___
study; however, the overall position of the fracture fragments is unchanged. 
There has been no significant interval change in the degree of distraction of
the fracture fragments.  No new fracture or acute subluxation of the cervical
spine is seen.  The atlanto-axial and atlanto-occipital articulations are well
maintained.

The overall cervical alignment is unchanged from ___.  Multilevel
degenerative changes are again noted with posterior disc osteophyte complexes
at the C5-C6 and C6-C7 levels, moderately narrowing the central canal.
Bilateral moderate to severe neural foraminal narrowing is also most
pronounced at C5-C6 and C6-C7 levels.

A left retropharyngeal hypodense mass is redemonstrated, now measuring 3.1 x
1.6 cm which is slightly increased in size from ___ and appears to deviate
the airway to the contralateral side.  The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  The
visualized lung apices are clear.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Chronic type II dens fracture with a single screw transfixing the
displaced odontoid fracture fragments which is overall unchanged in position
with no increased distraction of the fracture fragments, but increased lucency
at the tip of the screw compared to the prior ___ study suggesting loosening.
No new fracture or acute subluxation of the cervical spine is seen.
2.  Left retropharyngeal mass increased in size from ___, which appears to
deviate the airway.  If clinically indicated, further evaluation with MRI
would be indicated to better evaluate for interval change in this lesion which
again may be a post-inflammatory or unusual Tornwaldt's cyst.
3.  Multilevel cervical spondylosis.

INDICATION:  ___ female with history of neck fracture status post
mechanical fall, here to evaluate for acute intracranial process.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast head CT last performed on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the
brain.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were reviewed.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage, edema,
mass effect, or shift of normally midline structures.  Mild periventricular
white matter hypoattenuation is consistent with chronic small vessel ischemic
disease.  The gray-white matter interface is otherwise well preserved with no
evidence of acute major vascular territorial infarct.  The ventricles and
sulci are proportionally enlarged, compatible with age-related involutional
changes.  A ___ cisterna magna is incidentally noted.

The extracalvarial soft tissues are intact.  The bony calvarium and skull base
show no fracture.  The paranasal sinuses show mild ethmoid sinus disease.  The
mastoid air cells are well aerated. 

IMPRESSION:  
1.  No acute intracranial process.  
2.  Chronic small vessel ischemic disease and age-appropriate global atrophy
is noted.

INDICATION:  Mechanical fall.

COMPARISON:  ___.

LEFT SHOULDER, THREE VIEWS:  No fracture or dislocation is identified.  Marked
degenerative changes of the glenohumeral joint are noted with joint space
narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and marginal osteophytes.  There are no soft
tissue calcifications.  Visualized left lung demonstrates atelectatic changes
in the lung base.

IMPRESSION:  No acute fracture or dislocation.

INDICATION:  Mechanical fall.

COMPARISON:  ___.

SEMI-UPRIGHT AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  Heart size remains moderately enlarged. 
The mediastinal and hilar contours are stable.  The pulmonary vascularity is
not engorged.  Streaky linear opacities in the lung bases are most compatible
with subsegmental atelectasis.  More focal patchy opacity in the retrocardiac
region could represent area of atelectasis, though a developing infection
cannot be completely excluded.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax is
present.  Multiple old right-sided posterior rib fractures are noted.  No
acute displaced rib fractures are otherwise seen.

IMPRESSION:  Bibasilar subsegmental atelectasis.  More focal opacity in the
retrocardiac region likely represents another area of atelectasis, though
early infection is not excluded.  Multiple old right-sided rib fractures.

INDICATION:  Mechanical fall.

COMPARISON:  None.

LEFT ELBOW, THREE VIEWS:  There is a prominent anterior fat pad sign,
suggestive of an underlying joint effusion.  While no discrete fracture line
is visible, an occult radial head fracture cannot be excluded.  Mild
degenerative changes are noted within the elbow joint.  No focal lytic or
sclerotic osseous abnormality is seen.  There is no dislocation.

IMPRESSION:  Presence of a prominent anterior fat pad suggests an underlying
effusion and an occult radial head fracture cannot be excluded.  No discrete
fracture line, however, is visible.

INDICATION:  Mechanical fall with large hematoma and ecchymosis to the right
knee and mild swelling to the left knee.

COMPARISON:  Right knee radiographs, ___ and left knee
radiographs, ___.

BILATERAL KNEES, THREE VIEWS EACH:
On the right, there is no acute fracture or dislocation.  Extensive
prepatellar soft tissue swelling is noted along with a suprapatellar joint
effusion.  There are tricompartmental degenerative changes, most pronounced in
the lateral compartment with joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and
osteophyte formation.

On the left, no acute fracture or dislocation is present.  There
tricompartmental degenerative changes, similar to the prior study with joint
space narrowing, osteophyte formation, and subchondral sclerosis. Previously
noted chondrocalcinosis is not well seen. No sizable suprapatellar joint
effusion is visualized.  Soft tissue calcifications are again seen within the
anterior aspect of the knee.  No focal lytic or sclerotic osseous abnormality
seen.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Large prepatellar soft tissue swelling on the right with associated
suprapatellar joint effusion.
2.  No fracture or dislocation in either knee.

STUDY: THREE VIEWS OF THE LEFT HAND ___.

COMPARISON:  Left wrist radiographs ___.

INDICATION:  Status post mechanical fall, question fracture.

FINDINGS:  Unremarkable soft tissues.  Osteopenia which limits evaluation for
subtle fractures.  Degenerative changes are noted at the DIP and PIP joints
with joint space narrowing and some osseous proliferation.  Degenerative
changes of the MCP joints particularly the long and thumb with joint space
narrowing and sclerosis.  Moderate degenerative changes of the thumb CMC
joint, unchanged.  Mild ulnar negative variance unchanged.  No definite
fracture or dislocation.

IMPRESSION:  Degenerative changes as above.  No definite fracture.  If there
is continued concern, recommend MRI.
